d2.text: To protect your account, I have sent a 6-digit code to your registered WhatsApp number.

d4.text: I already paid, here is the screenshot.

d5.text: For your security, I can't help with this request in chat. A specialist from our team will review it.

d7.text: You will not receive further automated reminders from us on any channel.

p01.text: Every month, millions of people in India pay back a loan. And every month, their lender sends them the same reminder, at the same time, as everyone else.

p02.text: In one simulated campaign, that fixed schedule sent 1,262 messages, and paid for every one. Only 23 replies came back.

p04.text: Kairos works differently. Every morning, it looks at each borrower: how late they are, how they replied before, and when they usually read messages.

p05.text: Then it decides: reach out today, or wait. And if it reaches out, which channel, and at what hour.

p07.text: Before any message goes out, it has to get past Aladdin, our safety supervisor.

p08.text: Has this person agreed to this channel? Asked us to stop? Is it between 8 in the morning and 7 in the evening? Have we contacted them enough this week? Is there budget left? Is the account on hold?

p09.text: Aladdin checks when the message is planned, and again right before it is sent. If any answer is no, the message does not go.

p10.text: This is Vikram. His EMI of ₹7,409 is 10 days late. Kairos sends one SMS at 9:30 in the morning. No reply.

p11.text: So the next day, it waits. On day 3, it tries WhatsApp, and Vikram replies: he'll pay by the 29th.

p12.text: Kairos sees a promise to pay and goes quiet. On day 7, the bank confirms the payment. Reaching him cost 65 paise.

p13.text: Kairos learns from every reply. Midway through, we made WhatsApp work worse for one group and told Kairos nothing. Its estimate fell, and it moved that group to SMS on its own.

p15.text: Borrowers also write in on WhatsApp, at any hour. Kairos replies in seconds.

p16.text: Notice: nothing about her loan is shared until she proves who she is.

p17.text: That screenshot was edited. Kairos checks every proof against the bank's records, so a fake one goes to a person, never marks the loan paid.

p18.text: When another borrower says she has lost her job, Kairos pauses her reminders and hands her to a person.

p19.text: And when someone says stop, everything stops. SMS, WhatsApp, email and calls, all at once.

p20.text: The team stays in charge: approve a call, pause a borrower, take over a chat. And Aladdin checks them too. Not even a supervisor can send a message at 8 at night.

p22.text: In our simulated tests, Kairos recovered more for every rupee spent than a fixed schedule, without breaking a single rule.

c00.text: Kairos is a decision engine for loan collections. Every morning it decides, for each borrower, whether to make contact today, on which channel, and at what hour.

c01.text: Everything starts from one record per borrower: their loans, each EMI, every payment, their consent for each channel, and a log of every event. Money is stored in paise, the smallest unit, so totals never drift.

c02.text: Each morning, the churn engine sorts every borrower into groups: by cohort, risk, contact layer and status, using written rules. Every move records the rule that fired and the value it checked. Here, a borrower moves from medium to high risk because he is now more than 60 days late.

c03.text: The learner is a Bayesian model. For each group of borrowers, every channel and hour keeps a reply chance estimate with its uncertainty, updated when each message's 24-hour window closes. When we cut WhatsApp replies on day 7, its estimate fell from 13.5 to 9.7 in 100, and that group moved to SMS.

c04.text: Aladdin is the gate every message must pass. It checks consent, stop requests, contact hours, weekly limits, budget and holds, and reserves the budget in one atomic step, so two decisions can never spend the same rupee; then it checks again at send time. In a load test, 50,000 decisions went through in 11.1 seconds, with zero limit breaches.

c05.text: Adapters send each message, and each channel calls us back with what happened: a webhook. Repeats are ignored, a delivery never counts as a reply, and voice calls come back from AI voice agents with an outcome and a confidence. Kairos, not the agent, acts on it, and anything below a hand-set threshold waits for a person.

c06.text: Inbound chats run on a state machine, which means a chat can only move through a few allowed steps. Nothing about the account is shared until the borrower enters a one-time code, and edited or reused payment proofs go to a person. In 1,000 seeded test conversations, 73% were resolved without a person, and all 127 fakes were caught.

c08.text: People stay in charge: they can approve calls, pause borrowers and take over chats. Each action passes Aladdin and lands in the audit log. When an operator tries to send an SMS at 8 in the evening, Aladdin blocks it, and no role can override that.

c09.text: Same data and seed, same decisions. The replay matched exactly, 49 out of 49 attacks were stopped, and 3030 tests passed. From the logs alone, off policy evaluation estimated 18.2 replies per 1,000 messages against a true 18.4.

c10.text: None of this is magic. Each part stands on published research.

p06.text: All within a fixed daily budget, with a report every evening on what worked.
